document_check.note: Broadhouse KM, Winks NJ, Summers MJ. 'Fronto-temporal functional disconnection precedes hippocampal atrophy in clinically confirmed multi-domain amnestic mild cognitive impairment.' EXCLI Journal 2021;20:1458-1473, doi:10.17179/excli2021-4191. A cross-sectional structural and resting-state fMRI comparison of HC (n = 24), longitudinally confirmed mdaMCI (n = 14) and mild AD (n = 6). This matches the cited Broadhouse et al. 2021.

cited_result: The group comparison of HC versus clinically confirmed mdaMCI. Resting-state fronto-temporal (and whole-brain) ROI-to-ROI functional connectivity was significantly reduced in mdaMCI, while hippocampal subvolumes and vertex-wise cortical thickness did not differ significantly between HC and mdaMCI.
tool_reason: The cited result is a comparison of imaging measures between diagnostic groups at one time point, not a classifier's performance or a single test's accuracy against a reference standard.

domains.domain: Item 1: Criteria for inclusion clearly defined
domains.rationale: The main text gives the age threshold and the operational mdaMCI criterion. General eligibility and exclusion criteria are deferred to a supplementary file that is not part of the source document, and the healthy-control criteria are not set out in the main text.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: Recruitment and selection of participants is described in the supplementary information (Supplementary File 1).

domains.domain: Item 2: Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: Recruitment sources, the screening funnel (128 telephone-screened, 48 eligible) and group demographics (Table 2) are reported.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: Participants aged 65 years and older were recruited from the local community by referral from health care providers as well as volunteers from community-based groups for older adults.

domains.domain: Item 3: Exposure measured in a valid and reliable way (exposure = diagnostic group assignment)
domains.rationale: mdaMCI was confirmed by repeat full neuropsychological assessment one month apart, all performed by one experienced clinical neuropsychologist. One caveat: two 'possible mdaMCI' participants who did not meet criteria at reassessment were reclassified as healthy controls, and controls themselves were not reassessed.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: All possible mdaMCI cases underwent repeat full neuropsychological assessment 1 month later to confirm mdaMCI diagnosis. ... All assessments were carried out by the same registered Clinical Neuropsychologist with over 20 years of experience (MS).

domains.domain: Item 4: Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: mdaMCI was defined by an explicit psychometric cut-off applied at two time points, from the authors' published criteria. It is objective, though not the NIA-AA or Petersen consensus definition, and no biomarker was used.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: Criteria for mdaMCI was the presence of a subclinical impairment (>1.28SD below age-referent normative means)

domains.rationale: Age is explicitly identified as a confounder of brain structure and function. Sex, education, handedness, living status, alcohol and smoking were compared between groups.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: Although there was no significant difference in age between the groups, there is a significant correlation between age and brain structure and function

domains.domain: Item 6: Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated
domains.rationale: Age was entered as a covariate in all MRI group analyses, and head-motion, white-matter and CSF signals were regressed out of the functional data. Sex, education and premorbid IQ (WTAR FSIQ differed, HC > mdaMCI, p = .010) were not adjusted for, and group differences in head motion were not reported.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: age was included as a covariate in the subsequent analyses of MRI measures

domains.domain: Item 7: Outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way (outcome = hippocampal subvolume, cortical thickness, ROI-to-ROI connectivity)
domains.rationale: The study used 3T acquisition with standard FreeSurfer v6.0 and CONN pipelines, processed by an investigator blinded to group.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Processing and analysis of MRI data was undertaken by an experienced investigator (KB) who was blinded to the participant group.

domains.rationale: The tests are appropriate in form: ANCOVA with age, Bonferroni for hippocampal volumes, cluster-wise correction for thickness, and FDR for connectivity. However, the cited contrast (connectivity differs where structure does not) rests on non-significant structural results in 14 vs 24 participants, compared across analyses with very different multiplicity burdens. The adequacy claim relies on observed power from the demographic and neuropsychological table, not the MRI analyses. No test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals are given for the HC vs mdaMCI MRI results.

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: significant differences were detected where very large effect sizes were present (f > .387) indicating that the analyses were sufficiently powered to detect meaningful differences between group performances

overall: Some concerns (JBI analytical cross-sectional: items 1 and 8 Unclear; no item No)
overall_rationale: Group classification is rigorous and MRI processing was blinded. Age was adjusted for and motion regressed, so none of the four items that trigger High is answered No. Concerns remain because eligibility criteria sit in an unavailable supplement and the analysis supporting the cited contrast has gaps: the structural null is underpowered, MRI effect statistics are not reported, and the power claim comes from post hoc observed power. The authors acknowledge the small sample.

applicability.rationale: Only multi-domain amnestic MCI, confirmed psychometrically at two time points, without biomarker characterisation, in a small community-recruited Australian sample. The authors note the result may not extend to other MCI subtypes.
